approach: Add `Athena::propose_automatically(ui)` in proposals.rs. It wraps the existing `propose`, never returns an error, and prints a line on failure. It is silent when nothing is proposed. Call it from introspect_job and introspect_intervention once an introspection record is stored. Add a `Steps::propose` method with a no-op default, implemented by RealSteps through that wrapper, and call it first in `drain_with`. `generate` and its rules are untouched. The recorded proposals are the existing pending DefaultsProposal records, so `athena status` already lists them through `proposal_views`.

decisions.choice: Hook in introspect_job/introspect_intervention after a record is returned, not inside `introspect`.
decisions.reason: These two are the never-failing entry points used by run.rs, reading.rs and manage.rs. One hook covers every caller, and the introspection is already committed when proposing runs.

rejected.option: Hook in each caller (run.rs, reading.rs, manage.rs)
rejected.why: Three places, and a new caller could forget it.
A propose failure could then fail the introspection, which must never be blocked.

decisions.choice: Add `Steps::propose(&self)` with a default no-op body; RealSteps overrides it.
decisions.reason: The existing Stub implementations in tests keep compiling. Drain tests can use a counting stub to show propose runs at drain start, before the queue is read.

rejected.option: Call Athena::propose directly in main.rs before drain
rejected.why: Not testable through `drain()`, and it misses other callers of drain.

decisions.choice: Keep `generate` unchanged and rely on its rules for no-repeat.
decisions.reason: The brief puts the threshold and rejection rules out of scope. The existing rule already skips classes with a pending, accepted or rejected proposal.

rejected.why: Duplicates the rule and could drift from it.

files.purpose: Add `propose_automatically`, a never-failing, quiet-when-empty wrapper over `propose`. Note: the brief's propose.rs does not exist.
Call it after a record is stored in introspect_job and introspect_intervention; update the module docs.
Add `Steps::propose` with a no-op default, a RealSteps implementation, and a call at the start of drain_with; update the module docs.
Test for criteria 1 and 5 on the introspection side.
Tests for no re-proposal and status listing (criteria 2 and 3).
Tests for propose at drain start, the steward limit, and failure isolation.
Only if needed: the help text of drain and propose mentions the automatic run.
Only if the status test shows the proposal is not listed; expected to need no change.

steps: In proposals.rs, factor `propose` into a core that takes a `quiet_when_empty` flag, and add `propose_automatically(&self, ui)` that returns () and turns Err into a ui line such as 'automatic proposing failed: …'.
In introspect.rs, in introspect_job and introspect_intervention, call it when the settled result is Some, then return the record. Update the module docs.

In drain.rs, add `fn propose(&self, _ui: &dyn Ui) {}` to Steps, implement it in RealSteps through `self.athena.propose_automatically(self.ui)`, and call it at the top of drain_with before `steps.queue()`. Update the module docs.

Add tests. In introspection.rs: threshold crossed produces a pending proposal, and a failing propose does not fail the introspection. In proposals.rs: no re-proposal for pending, accepted or rejected classes, and the status listing. In drain.rs: a counting stub, and a real-steps drain with in-limit and above-limit items.
Add the CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entry and touch main.rs help text if it describes propose.
Run cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: A propose failure or a slow `read_records` blocks an introspection or drain.
risks.mitigation: The wrapper catches every error and prints one line. Tests cover introspect_job and drain.

risks.risk: Every introspection prints 'no class has repeated', which is noisy.
risks.mitigation: The wrapper suppresses the 'no class has repeated' line and prints only when proposals were written or refused.

risks.risk: Extra commits during a job run conflict with the job's own record commits.
risks.mitigation: Use existing test helpers that seed records. Check that commit_records is safe under the existing run-time commit path; commit only when proposals are non-empty.

risks.risk: Adding a trait method breaks the existing Steps impls in tests.
risks.mitigation: Have the stub default propose as a no-op. Run the whole drain test file.

demonstrations.method: Test in tests/introspection.rs. Record introspections for one class on threshold-1 distinct jobs and check there is no proposal. Then record the threshold-reaching one through introspect_job. Never call athena.propose.
demonstrations.observes: The records hold exactly one pending DefaultsProposal for the class.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the hook in introspect_job, no proposal exists after the threshold-reaching introspection, so the assertion on a pending proposal fails.

demonstrations.method: Tests in tests/proposals.rs. After the automatic proposal exists, run another introspection of the class and a drain-start propose, and count proposals. Repeat for a rejected class with fewer than N newer distinct jobs, and for an accepted class.
demonstrations.observes: The proposal count stays at 1 each time, or 0 new for the rejected class.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the hook bypassed generate's rules, a second proposal would appear for the pending or rejected class.

demonstrations.method: Create the proposal automatically as in criterion 1, then build the status report and render it.
demonstrations.observes: The status proposals list and rendered text name the new proposal's class and id.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without automatic proposing, the status text has no proposal entry.

demonstrations.method: Test in tests/drain.rs. A stub counts propose calls and checks that the call happens before the queue is read. A second test on the real repository seeds a class at threshold, runs drain, and checks the proposal is pending and that an in-limit work item is approved and worked while an above-limit one is listed as waiting.
demonstrations.observes: One propose call before queue(); the in-limit item is approved and run; the above-limit item is in the report's waiting list.
demonstrations.fails_without: If drain did not call Steps::propose at start, the counting stub records zero calls and the real-steps test finds no proposal.

demonstrations.method: Tests with a failing propose (for example an unreadable record that makes `read_records` fail, or a stub whose propose reports an error). Check that introspect_job still returns the record, drain returns Ok, and the failure line is printed through the Ui. Then run the three check commands.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --all --check
demonstrations.observes: The record is returned, the report is Ok, the output contains the proposing failure line, and all three commands exit 0.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the error propagated, the introspection or drain would return an error or None where the test expects the record or Report.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the diff. CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased entry on automatic proposing, and the module docs of introspect.rs and drain.rs mention it.
demonstrations.observes: The diff touches only the listed Rust files and CHANGELOG.md. defaults.toml, athena.toml and the workflows are absent from it.

open_questions: Defaults proposals (DefaultsProposal) are separate from steward work items (WorkItem). The code has no path that approves a defaults proposal under the steward limit. Criterion 4 therefore cannot be met literally for them. The plan covers propose at drain start, with the existing in-limit and above-limit work-item handling unchanged. The user should confirm that reading.
How many distinct jobs is the threshold? The test must read it from generate's constant in proposals.rs.
Should an introspection run during a drain trigger propose while jobs run concurrently? Commits go through commit_records, whose locking was not checked.
